B.fault: Neither the facts nor the quoted rule text says China is in Country Group D:5. The presumption-of-denial sentence is keyed to Macau and D:5 destinations, so answer B relies on outside knowledge that China is D:5. If China were not D:5, the quoted text would set no default policy. Minor; the intended and legally correct answer is still B.
Same gap as licence-review-04: China's membership in Country Group D:5 is not stated in the facts or quoted rule text, and the presumption-of-denial sentence depends on it. Minor; the answer stays B.
Very minor: no date is given, yet the quoted NY text is 'in effect January 1, 2027'. The question asks under the Act as amended, so the answer is A either way.

Minor wording risk. The question asks which paragraph the chip 'meets'. Read as a bare parametric match, b.1 (option C) is met numerically (TPP 3000 in 2400..<4800, PD 2.5 in 1.6..<5.92). Note 2 in the rule text removes 3A090.a and b for items not designed or marketed for datacenters with TPP under 4800, so E is the intended and better answer, but 'meet' invites the C reading.

The answer (B, presumption of denial) needs China to be in Country Group D:5, or otherwise caught by the 'all other applications' sentence. Neither the facts nor the quoted rule text says China is in D:5; the quoted sentence names only Macau and D:5 destinations. A reader limited to the file can rule out A (TPP 22,400 is not below 21,000) and C (nothing supports approval) but cannot derive B from the text alone. It is also not stated whether the 'all other' sentence covers an end user located in China at all.

A.fault: Minor wording risk. 'Which paragraphs ... does the chip meet' can be read as 'which paragraphs' numeric parameters does the chip satisfy'. On that reading the chip meets b.1 (TPP 3000 in [2400, 4800), PD 2.5 in [1.6, 5.92)) and a reader would pick C. Note 2 is quoted and says a and b do not apply to this chip, so E is the better answer. Asking which paragraph, if any, 'covers' or 'applies to' the chip would remove the doubt.

The facts do not say whether the parent's $290,000,000 is its own standalone revenue or a consolidated figure that already includes its subsidiaries' $240,000,000 (180M + 60M). Read as standalone, which is the natural reading and fits 'none of that revenue came from sales among them', the total is $530M and the answer is A.
